claims.text: POL-NS-23 voids a no-show fee unless the driver, before cancelling, sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call. The trip record's contact_before_cancel block (EV-TRIP-05053) shows call_count 2 but message_count 0 with an empty messages array, and sets obligation_met false. The driver never sent a single in-app message before the 12:21:10 cancellation, so the message limb is unmet and the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided: the rider is not charged.

The only chat entry on this trip (EV-CHAT-05053) is the rider's own message, 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 - 40 seconds AFTER the driver cancelled at 12:21:10. It cannot count as a driver message sent before cancelling, so the chat log confirms rather than cures the missing message limb of POL-NS-23.

The rider's own account concedes he did not answer the calls ('my phone was on silent'), and the record agrees: both in-app calls went unanswered (answered false, 20 s and 18 s, at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40). But POL-NS-23 is conjunctive - it requires a message AND a call - and whether the rider answered the call is not part of the test. Two unanswered calls cannot supply the missing message limb, which is fatal to the fee on its own.

The driver's counterparty statement is 'I called two times, no answer.' It asserts calls only and says nothing about any in-app chat message, which is consistent with a chat log carrying zero driver messages. Nothing in the record - not the trip record, not the chat log, not the driver's own account - supplies the message limb POL-NS-23 requires.

The rider does not dispute the free wait, and does not need to: the driver's arrival at 12:15:30 is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 3.07 m from the pickup at 12:16:44, accuracy 6.0 m, inside the STANDARD 50 m arrival radius) and the 12:21:10 cancellation came 340 s later, past the 300 s free wait. That does not save the fee. POL-NS-21 (free wait) and POL-NS-23 (contact obligation) are separate, cumulative requirements, and the rider's entitlement rests on the contact obligation, which fails independently of the wait.

POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome operates only 'where the fee stands'. POL-NS-23 removes the fee where the contact obligation is unmet, and it says expressly that the rider is not charged and there is no driver compensation. There is therefore nothing for the driver to receive: the ruling is FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD fee charged and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

The remedy is the return of the whole contested sum. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05053) shows exactly one line, a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged at 12:21:14, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0, with fee_matches_policy true. Voiding that fee under POL-NS-23 means the filing rider is entirely right and the full 5.00 SGD is returned: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 under POL-GEN-03.

claims.text: The driver arrived at the pickup at 12:15:30 and cancelled at 12:21:10, after the 300-second free wait required by POL-NS-21, so the no-show fee of 5.00 SGD is properly chargeable under POL-NS-22.

The driver placed two in-app calls to the rider, at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40, both before cancellation. The rider admits the calls in their own claim text. This satisfies the call requirement of POL-NS-23.

The rider's own message 'Coming down now, sorry' was sent at 12:21:50, after the free wait expired and after the driver cancelled. This confirms the rider was not at the pickup point and was a genuine no-show.

The rider's claim that no in-app chat message was sent is true, but the driver's two in-app calls, which the rider admits, constitute sufficient contact under POL-NS-23. The rider's phone was on silent, so a chat message would have been equally ineffective. The missing message is not a ground to void the fee where the driver made reasonable and repeated contact attempts.

The rider was notified by the platform push at 12:15:34 ('Your driver has arrived'), and the driver called twice; the rider's later apology shows they were aware of the driver's presence. The fee should stand as the rider failed to board within the free wait.

The rider's claim is not supported because the driver's two in-app calls, admitted by the rider, satisfied the contact obligation in substance, and the rider's own late message confirms they were a no-show. The present state should stand.

If the no-show fee stands, the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00, as the fee was properly charged and transferred to the driver under POL-NS-22.

ruling.explanation:
You were charged a 5.00 SGD no-show fee when the driver cancelled TRP-05053 at 12:21:10. The rider's dispute succeeds, and the whole 5.00 SGD is returned.

The reason is POL-NS-23, the driver's contact obligation. Before cancelling for a no-show, the driver must have BOTH sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, each before cancellation. The record shows the calls were made — two in-app calls at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40, both unanswered, both before the 12:21:10 cancellation (EV-TRIP-05053). But the message limb fails: the chat log (EV-CHAT-05053) contains no driver message at all, and the trip record's contact check (EV-TRIP-05053) reports message_count 0 and obligation_met false. The only message on the trip is the rider's own 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 — 40 seconds after the cancellation — so it cannot be a driver message sent before cancelling. POL-NS-23 is conjunctive: the missing message alone voids the fee. The driver's argument that the two calls and the push notification amounted to reasonable contact cannot override the clause's plain requirement of both a message and a call, and whether the rider's phone was on silent does not change the test.

The free wait under POL-NS-21 was in fact satisfied (arrival 12:15:30, cancellation 340 s later, past the 300 s free wait), but POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-23 are separate, cumulative conditions, and a fee the contact obligation voids cannot be resurrected by the wait. POL-NS-22's driver compensation applies only 'where the fee stands', so the driver receives nothing here.

The money figures are read from the fare ledger (EV-FARE-05053): 5.00 SGD charged, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 the rider is entirely right, so this is a FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with driver_compensation_sgd null.

No referral fires. The fee charged was exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not apply; the driver did attempt contact, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not apply; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show counter is not present on the rider profile (and the fee does not stand in any event).

The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD first band, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final.

Because the message limb is missing, the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged (EV-FARE-05053) is voided. You are refunded the full 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation. To the driver: I accept that you arrived at 12:15:30 and waited past the 300-second free wait before cancelling at 12:21:10, and that the GPS trace corroborates your arrival. I also accept that you called twice. But POL-NS-23 is cumulative: the calls cannot replace the required in-app chat message. The rider's late message, your counterparty statement, and the platform push notification do not satisfy that message requirement. Since the fee does not stand, POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome does not apply. Confidence is 0.95, based on the complete trip record and chat log, both at full weight.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-05053 is voided and returned to you in full, so amount_sgd is 5.00 and driver_compensation_sgd is null. The governing clause is POL-NS-23 (the driver's contact obligation), which requires that, before cancelling for a no-show, the driver both sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call. The trip record EV-TRIP-05053 (contact_before_cancel) shows call_count 2 but message_count 0 with an empty messages array and sets obligation_met false; the chat log EV-CHAT-05053 carries exactly one entry, your own message at 12:21:50, which is 40 seconds after the 12:21:10 cancellation. The message limb is therefore unmet, and POL-NS-23 voids the fee with no driver compensation. The fare ledger EV-FARE-05053 confirms the sums: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The free-wait requirement in POL-NS-21 was in fact satisfied - the driver's arrival at 12:15:30 is corroborated by the GPS trace EV-GPS-05053 (nearest fix 3.07 m from the pickup at 12:16:44, accuracy 6.0 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) and the 12:21:10 cancellation came 340 s later, past the 300 s free wait - but POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-23 are separate and cumulative requirements, and the fee does not survive the contact obligation. To the driver: your two in-app calls at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40 are on the record and the rider does not deny them, but POL-NS-23 is conjunctive - a message is required as well as a call - so two unanswered calls cannot carry the fee, and the rider's phone being on silent does not change the clause's test. Your counterparty statement ('I called two times, no answer') asserts calls only and says nothing about any message, which is consistent with the zero-message record. No referral is produced: the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD in POL-NS-22, the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter for POL-NS-25, and POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire because the driver did arrive and did attempt contact. Confidence 0.95; the deciding facts rest on EV-TRIP-05053 and EV-CHAT-05053, both weight 1.0.

To the rider and the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee is voided and returned to the rider, and the driver receives no compensation.

Why. POL-NS-23 sets a two-part contact obligation the driver must meet BEFORE cancelling for a no-show: he must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The clause is conjunctive — 'if either is missing, the fee is voided.' The record shows only half of it. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05053, weight 1.0) carries a contact_before_cancel block with call_count 2 but message_count 0, an empty messages array, and obligation_met false. The platform chat log (EV-CHAT-05053, weight 1.0) holds exactly one entry — the rider's own 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50, forty seconds AFTER the 12:21:10 cancellation — so it cannot be a driver message sent before cancelling. The driver's own account ('I called two times, no answer') speaks only of calls. Nothing in the record supplies the missing message limb, so the fee is voided under POL-NS-23 and the rider is not charged.

The rider's side is accepted: the message limb of POL-NS-23 was never met; the single chat entry is the rider's post-cancellation message and cannot cure it; the two unanswered calls (answered false, 20 s at 12:17:55 and 18 s at 12:19:40) satisfy the call limb only; and POL-NS-22's DRIVER_COMPENSATION outcome operates only 'where the fee stands', which it does not, so driver_compensation_sgd is null. The evidence supporting all this sits on artifacts at weight 1.0 each (EV-TRIP-05053 and EV-CHAT-05053), so nothing impairs the finding.

The driver's points are answered, and most do not decide the fee. I accept the timing facts: the driver's arrival at 12:15:30 is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 3.07 m away at 12:16:44, accuracy 6.0 m, inside the STANDARD 50 m radius) and the 12:21:10 cancellation came 340 s later, past the 300 s free wait, so POL-NS-21 was met and the two calls did satisfy the call limb of POL-NS-23; the rider's late apology does show he was late to board; and the platform did send the 'Your driver has arrived' push at 12:15:34. But none of that decides the case, because POL-NS-21 (free wait) and POL-NS-23 (contact obligation) are separate, cumulative requirements, and the fee falls on POL-NS-23 independently of the wait. I reject the argument that the two calls are 'sufficient contact in substance' under POL-NS-23: the clause is explicit that a message AND a call are both required and that a missing one voids the fee, and the rider's phone being on silent is not part of that test. I likewise reject the contention that the present state should stand and the driver's claim to 5.00 SGD compensation — both depend on the fee standing, and it does not.

Money. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05053, weight 1.0) shows one line only, a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged at 12:21:14, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0. Under POL-GEN-03 that whole contested sum is returned: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd 5.00 and driver_compensation_sgd null.

Referrals. None. The POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not fire because the driver did attempt contact (the two calls). POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not fire: the fee does not stand and the named field is not present on the rider profile. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire because the amount charged (5.00 SGD) matches the policy fee.

Confidence and who decides. This is a 5.00 SGD dispute, below POL-GEN-22's first band, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at any confidence. No safety flag and no fraud flag is present, so no escalation arises.
